title: Independently certify all-sequence retired-lender exhaustion
body:
PR2559 reports nine possible retired-lender pairs on the PR2526 words, at most two stack, and none remain after its chosen aliases. This independently certifies the all-sequence implication: under the precisely stated ordinary one-warp retired-lender class, substitutions cannot create a candidate outside the initial set. A common lifetime interval then forces a graph matching of size at most two. The existing shipped selection reaches that ceiling under its retained native-admission assumptions.

The existing count, maximum-two claim and construction are credited to Philippe Van Velzen/PR2559. New coverage is the independent necessary census and noncreation/interval proof, rather than another endpoint or root replay. The two initial words are pinned at `113c427bf6abe2572184621ebfa00ce7cdf06c46`; the two shipped words at `383ce6c84d92b7b3f00fe267cb23bf3233eecc77`. All retained bytes carry SHA256/Git blob pins.

The primary represents GF(2)^9 subspaces by complete sets of 512 vectors and uses exact integer event slots. It relaxes the predecessor's terminal containment test to dimension capacity, obtaining the same nine necessary pairs. A separate per-role binary-elimination interpreter agrees on all four words. All five candidate helper lifetimes overlap; the graph has sixteen size-two matchings. Those matchings are combinatorial possibilities, not sixteen newly admitted native words.

The checker also binds every changed field of the shipped two-alias word, both invertible binary warp maps and their frame images, all inverse cleanup instructions, and the full frame/profile ledger. The original paid delta `+H1-2H5` is reproduced. Six semantic controls reject conflicting lifetimes, duplicate helper removal, singular/wrong-image warps, missing cleanup and an omitted rank-one climb. Equivalent frame bases pass.

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/retired-lender-exhaustion
python3.12 -I -O -B research/retired-lender-exhaustion/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/retired-lender-exhaustion/check_integrity.py
```

Registered CPython3.12.14 replay and Git-free read-only/source/typed-receipt/exclusive-output controls pass. A separate Codex reviewer read the proof/code and independently replayed the primary under CPython3.12.7: `words=4 initial_pairs=9 maximum=2 matchings=16 controls=6`, with no material issue.

This is a fixed-class exhaustion certificate, not a general helper minimum or new supplier/kappa. Lifted-target compensation, source-partner recovery, lifetime splitting, altered frames, changed terminal labels and different words are outside its hypotheses. Full native endpoints, owner fill and global/outer admission are inherited from PR2559 and not rerun here. No new physical price or conditional frontier claim is made. Open next questions identify what would be needed to test other matchings or escape the class.

Task `independent-moment`, seed `4befc9c886d4d27dc01247ae04bf4145`, changed scope recorded in TASK.json. Fresh canonical main remains `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority4; the binding baseline passed. Final overlap covers 766 open PRs at 2026-10-15T14:56:29Z plus local notes; the last complete Discussion snapshot has 1,197 records at 12:29Z and is explicitly stale after API rate limiting. Exact main and relevant heads were rechecked.

Credit Philippe Van Velzen/PR2559, Jeremy Kothe/PR2526, Tekalign/PR2436, Cinna Davis/PR2226 and the retained T74/native/global lineage. Prepared by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, proof, implementation, validation and prose. Separate AI review is not independent human review or maintainer admission. Apache-2.0; source notices retained; no hosted-CI pass claimed.
